For reproducibility, proceed exactly as follows: first equilibrate the walkers with pos = metropolis(configs, wf, tau=0.5, nsteps=2000) (the function from the earlier step); compute local energies eloc = wf.kinetic(pos) + ham.potential(pos) and initialize E_T = np.mean(eloc). Then for each of the nstep iterations: (1) chi = np.random.normal(size=pos.shape); (2) drift_old = tau*wf.gradient(pos), posnew = pos + np.sqrt(tau)*chi + drift_old, drift_new = tau*wf.gradient(posnew); (3) acc = get_acceptance_ratio(pos, posnew, drift_old, drift_new, tau, wf), u = np.random.random(nconf), accept the walkers where acc > u; (4) recompute elocnew on the updated positions; (5) weight = np.exp(-tau*((eloc + elocnew)/2 - E_T)); (6) append np.mean(elocnew) to the returned energies BEFORE branching; (7) idx = branch(weight), keep pos[idx] and eloc = elocnew[idx]; (8) E_T = E_T - np.log(np.mean(weight)).
